'''Kotohira Shrine''' (金刀比羅神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|abstract|Q812767|af|Sjintoïsme|an|Xintoísmo|anp|शिन्तो धर्म|ar|شنتو|ary|شينطو|arz|شنتو|as|শ্বিণ্ট'|ast|Sintoísmu|az|Şintoizm|azb|شینتوئیسم|ba|Синтоизм|bat_smg|Šintoėzmos|bcl|Shinto|be|Сінтаізм|be_x_old|Сінтаізм|bg|Шинтоизъм|blk|ဆိဉ်တိုဘာႏသာႏ|bn|শিন্তৌ ধর্ম|bo|ཧྲིན་ཐོ།|br|Shintoegezh|bs|Šintoizam|bxr|Синто|ca|Xintoisme|ckb|شینتۆ|cs|Šintoismus|cy|Shintō|da|Shinto|de|Shintō|diq|Şinto|el|Σιντοϊσμός|eo|Ŝintoo|es|Sintoísmo|et|Šintoism|eu|Sintoismo|ext|Sintoísmu|fa|شینتو|fi|Šintolaisuus|fiu_vro|Sinto|fr|Shintoïsme|fur|Sintoisim|fy|Sjintoïsme|gcr|Shintoyism|gd|Shinto|gl|Xintoísmo|gn|Sinto|got|𐍃𐌹𐌽𐍄𐍉|gu|શિન્તો|ha|Shinto|he|שינטו|hi|शिन्तो धर्म|hif|Shinto|hr|Šintoizam|hu|Sintó|hy|Սինտոիզմ|ia|Shinto|id|Shinto|io|Shinto|is|Sjintóismi|it|Shintoismo|ja|神道|jam|Shinto|jv|Shinto|ka|შინტოიზმი|kbp|Sinto|kg|Kisinto|kk|Синтоизм|km|ស៊ិនតូ|kn|ಶಿಂಟೋ ಧರ್ಮ|ko|신토|ks|شِنتو|ky|Шинто|la|Sintoismus|lad|Shintoizmo|lb|Shintō|lfn|Xinto|lij|Scintoiximo|lt|Šintoizmas|lv|Sintoisms|map_bms|Shinto|mg|Sintôisma|min|Shinto|mk|Шинтоизам|ml|ഷിന്റൊ|mn|Шинто|mni|ꯁꯤꯟꯇꯣ ꯂꯥꯢꯅꯤꯡ|mr|शिंतो धर्म|ms|Shinto|mt|Xintù|mwl|Xintoísmo|my|ရှင်တိုဘာသာ|nds|Shintō|new|शिन्तो धर्म|nl|Shintoïsme|nn|Shinto|no|Shintōisme|oc|Sintoïsme|olo|Šintolaižus|or|କାମିନୋ ମିଚି|pa|ਸ਼ਿੰਤੋਵਾਦ|pl|Shintō|pms|Shintoism|pnb|شنتو|ps|شينتو|pt|Xintoísmo|ro|Șintoism|ru|Синтоизм|rue|Сінтоїзм|sc|Shintoismu|scn|Shintuismu|sco|Shinto|sd|شنٽو|sh|Šintoizam|simple|Shinto|sk|Šintoizmus|sl|Šintoizem|sn|Ushintho|so|Shiintismi|sq|Shinto|sr|Шинтоизам|sv|Shinto|sw|Shinto|ta|சிந்தோ|te|షింటో మతం|tg|Шинто|th|ชินโต|tl|Shinto|tly|Sintoizm|tok|nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto|tt|Щинто|tyv|Синтоизм|uk|Синто|ur|شنتو|uz|Sintoizm|vi|Thần đạo|war|Shinto|wuu|神道|xmf|სინტოიზმი|yi|שינטא|yo|Shinto|za|Saenzdaugyau|zgh|ⵜⴰⵛⵉⵏⵟⵓⵜ|zh|神道|zh_min_nan|Sîn-tō|zh_yue|神道|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Seimicho|ja|勢見町|qid=Q11400568}}, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture. Situated at the base of {{ill|Mount Bizan|arz|جبل مونت بيزان|fr|Mont Bizan|ja|眉山 (徳島市)|lld|Mont Bizan|my|ဘိဇန်တောင်|uk|Бідзан (Токусіма)|qid=Q8189109|lt=Mt. Bizan}}, it is one of the three significant {{ill|Kotohira shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|lt=Kotohira Shrines}} in Tokushima Prefecture, alongside those in {{ill|Kawauchichō|ja|川内町 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawauchichō, Tokushima City|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11477745}} and {{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|en|Naruto, Tokushima|qid=Q460812|lt=Naruto City}}. Locals affectionately refer to it as the "Kotohira of Seimi."

The shrine grounds house Japan’s largest stone lantern, standing 10.24 meters tall, which has been designated a {{ill|Q11273094|ja|とくしま市民遺産|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Heritage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11273094}}.

== History ==

The shrine was relocated in {{ill|1616|en|1616|qid=Q6788|lt=1616}} (Genna 2) when {{ill|Hachisuka Iemasa|en|Hachisuka Iemasa|qid=Q1073557|lt=Hachisuka Iemasa}} entered {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|be|Ава (правінцыя, Сікоку)|cs|Provincie Awa (Tokušima)|de|Provinz Awa (Tokushima)|es|Provincia de Awa (Tokushima)|fa|ولایت آوا|fr|Province d'Awa (Tokushima)|gl|Provincia de Awa, Tokushima|id|Provinsi Awa (Tokushima)|it|Awa (provincia, Tokushima)|ja|阿波国|ko|아와국 (난카이도)|lt|Avos žemė (Tokušima)|nl|Awa (Tokushima)|pt|Província de Awa (Tokushima)|ru|Ава (Сикоку)|simple|Awa Province (Tokushima)|sk|Awa (provincia, Tokušima)|sr|Провинција Ава (Шикоку)|tr|Awa (vilayet, Tokushima)|uk|Провінція Ава (Шікоку)|zh|阿波國|zh_min_nan|Awa-kok (Nankaidô)|qid=Q907457|lt=Awa Province}} and established it as a tutelary shrine for {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|qid=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle}}. The nearby {{ill|seimiyama|ja|勢見山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seimi Mountain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11400566}} derives its name from an incident in which {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|en|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|qid=Q310445|lt=Minamoto no Yoshitsune}} surveyed enemy forces on his way to {{ill|Yashima|ja|屋島|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yashima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11465681}}. Originally, the mountain referred to {{ill|hachibuseyama|ja|鉢伏山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachibuse Mountain|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11649837}}, where {{ill|Katsura Shrine|ja|勝占神社}} resides, but the name migrated with the shrine's relocation.

Between 1885 (Meiji 18) and 1892 (Meiji 25), the {{ill|Inbe Shrine|en|Inbe Shrine|qid=Q11490722|lt=Inbe Shrine}} was temporarily enshrined here as a {{ill|Kokuhei Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}. Details of this period can be found in the {{ill|Inbe Shrine|en|Inbe Shrine|qid=Q11490722|lt=Inbe Shrine}} entry.

The grand torii was built in {{ill|1791|en|1791|qid=Q7784|lt=1791}} (Kansei 3), featuring the largest shimenawa in Tokushima Prefecture. Together with the {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Kawauchichō)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市川内町)}} and the {{ill|Kotohira Shrine (Naruto)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (鳴門市)}}, it is one of the “Awa San Konpira” (Three Kotohira Shrines of Awa).<ref>''History Walks of Tokushima Prefecture'' (2009, Yamakawa Shuppansha, p. 105)</ref>

== Access ==

* By bus: Take the Tokushima City Bus bound for "Nikenya・Hōge" from {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|qid=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station}} on the {{ill|Kōtoku Line|en|Kōtoku Line|qid=Q859984|lt=Kōtoku Line}} and alight at "Kotohira Shita," immediately outside the shrine.
* By train: Approximately 13 minutes on foot from {{ill|Niken'ya Station|en|Niken'ya Station|qid=Q10880415|lt=Nikenya Station}} on the {{ill|Mugi Line|en|Mugi Line|qid=Q860478|lt=Mugi Line}}.

Situated at the base of {{ill|Mount Bizan|arz|جبل مونت بيزان|fr|Mont Bizan|ja|眉山 (徳島市)|lld|Mont Bizan|my|ဘိဇန်တောင်|uk|Бідзан (Токусіма)|qid=Q8189109|lt=Mt. Bizan}}, it is affectionately known as "Seko's Konpira-san." It is one of the three major Kotohira Shrines in Tokushima Prefecture, alongside those in {{ill|Kawauchichō|ja|川内町 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawauchi Town, Tokushima City|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11477745}} and {{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|en|Naruto, Tokushima|qid=Q460812|lt=Naruto City}}, specifically in {{ill|Q11498695|ja|撫養町木津|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizucho, Naruto City|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498695}}.

The shrine grounds feature the largest stone lantern in Japan, standing 10.24 meters tall, which has been selected as a {{ill|Q11273094|ja|とくしま市民遺産|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Civic Heritage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11273094}}.

== History ==
The shrine was moved to its current location in {{ill|1616|en|1616|qid=Q6788|lt=1616}} (Genwa 2) after {{ill|Hachisuka Iemasa|en|Hachisuka Iemasa|qid=Q1073557|lt=Hachisuka Iemasa}} entered [[Awa Province]] and established {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|qid=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle}}. It was originally relocated from {{ill|Katsura chō|ja|勝占町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kachiden Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11400186}} as the tutelary shrine for the castle town. The nearby {{ill|seimiyama|ja|勢見山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mt. Seimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11400566}} derives its name from a legend in which {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|en|Minamoto no Yoshitsune|qid=Q310445|lt=Minamoto no Yoshitsune}} surveyed his troops en route to {{ill|Yashima|ja|屋島|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yashima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11465681}} after landing in Katsuura.

From {{ill|1885|en|1885|qid=Q7821|lt=1885}} (Meiji 18) to {{ill|1892|en|1892|qid=Q7839|lt=1892}} (Meiji 25), the shrine temporarily housed the {{ill|Inbe Shrine|en|Inbe Shrine|qid=Q11490722|lt=Imibe Shrine}}, which was designated a {{ill|National Middle Shrine|ja|国幣中社}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|modern shrine Ranking system]]. For more details, refer to the article on {{ill|Inbe Shrine|en|Inbe Shrine|qid=Q11490722|lt=Imibe Shrine}}.

The grand torii gate was constructed in {{ill|1791|en|1791|qid=Q7784|lt=1791}} (Kansei 3), and the shrine's shimenawa (sacred rope) is the largest in Tokushima Prefecture. Together with the Kotohira Shrines in Kawauchi and Naruto, the shrine has been historically referred to as one of the "Three Kotohira Shrines of Awa."<ref>"Tokushima History Walk" (2009, Yamakawa Publishing, p.105)</ref>

== City's Five Shrines ==
* {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} - Located in [[Minami Sako Sanbancho]], Tokushima City.
* {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|春日神社 (徳島市)}} - Located on Mt. Ōtaki, [[Bizan Town]], Tokushima City.
* {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)}} - Located in [[Iga Town, Tokushima City]].
* {{ill|Shisho Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|四所神社 (徳島市)}} - Located in [[Fukushima, Tokushima City]].

== Access ==
* From {{ill|JR|en|JR|qid=Q127942|lt=JR}} {{ill|Kōtoku Line|en|Kōtoku Line|qid=Q859984|lt=Kōtoku Line}}'s {{ill|Tokushima Station|en|Tokushima Station|qid=Q860775|lt=Tokushima Station}}, take the Tokushima City Bus bound for "Nikoya/Hokka" and get off at "Kotohira Shita." The shrine is a short walk from the stop.
* Approximately 13 minutes on foot from {{ill|JR|en|JR|qid=Q127942|lt=JR}} {{ill|Mugi Line|en|Mugi Line|qid=Q860478|lt=Mugi Line}}'s [[Nikoya Station]].
